paragraphs.title: David’s Prayer in the Face of His Enemies’ Hatred

easy.explanation: David addresses God, saying, “O God of my praise.”
easy.q: To whom does David speak at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me.”
easy.q: What did the wicked and deceitful open against David?

easy.explanation: David says, “but I give myself unto prayer.”
easy.q: What was David’s response to his enemies’ hatred?

answers: They repaid evil and hatred for good and love
medium.explanation: They “rewarded” him evil for good and hatred for his love.
medium.q: How did David’s enemies treat him?

medium.explanation: A lying tongue speaks words that are not true.
medium.q: What does the phrase “a lying tongue” describe?

answers: His enemies surround him with hatred and fight against him
He wants to leave his people
medium.explanation: David describes hateful words and enemies who fight against him without a cause.
medium.q: Why does David ask God not to hold His peace?

answers: They speak while he is silent
They return hatred, while he gives himself to prayer
They are poor while he is rich
challenge.explanation: The enemies repay love with hatred, while David responds through prayer.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between David and his enemies?

answers: They fought him without a stated just reason
They asked him for a gift
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that their attack had no cause or justification.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the phrase “fought against me without a cause”?

answers: To show the moral difference between his conduct and theirs
To prove that he does not pray
challenge.explanation: David loved them, but they answered his love with evil and hatred.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of mentioning David’s love alongside his enemies’ hatred?

easy.explanation: The curse says, “When he shall be judged, let him be condemned.”
easy.q: What do the enemies wish would happen to the man when he is judged?

easy.explanation: They say, “Let his days be few.”
easy.q: What do they wish would happen to his days?

answers: His wife would be a widow and his children fatherless
They would all leave the land
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.”
easy.q: What is said about his wife and children?

answers: An extortioner and strangers would take them
He would freely give them to the poor
medium.explanation: They ask that the extortioner catch all he has and that strangers spoil his labour.
medium.q: What do the enemies wish would happen to the man’s possessions?

answers: One who takes money or property unjustly
medium.explanation: An extortioner is someone who obtains possessions by force or unjust demands.
medium.q: What is an “extortioner” in this passage?

answers: Like clothing and a girdle continually upon him
medium.explanation: The curse is compared to a garment covering him and a girdle around him continually.
medium.q: How is the curse pictured as affecting the man?

answers: His life, family, possessions, and memory
challenge.explanation: The curses concern his days, family, property, descendants, and reputation.
challenge.q: Which areas of life are affected by the sequence of curses?

answers: That the enemies want no memory of him to remain
That they want to make his name famous
That they want him to teach
challenge.explanation: To have one’s name blotted out means to lose remembrance in future generations.
challenge.q: What is implied by the request that his name be blotted out?

answers: As one who shows mercy to everyone
As one who persecutes the poor, needy, and brokenhearted
As one who protects the weak
challenge.explanation: They accuse him of persecuting the poor and needy and slaying the broken in heart.
challenge.q: How do the enemies portray the man?

paragraphs.title: The Plea of the Poor and Persecuted

easy.explanation: David asks the Lord to act for His name’s sake and to deliver him.
easy.q: From whom does David ask for mercy and deliverance?

easy.explanation: He says, “For I am poor and needy.”
The KJV says, “when they looked upon me they shaked their heads.”
easy.q: What did David’s enemies do when they looked upon him?

medium.explanation: He says his knees are weak through fasting and his flesh fails of fatness.
medium.q: What physical conditions does David describe?

answers: His heart is full of joy
He is inwardly hurt and weak
medium.explanation: The phrase describes David’s deep inward suffering and weakness.
medium.q: What does “my heart is wounded within me” mean in context?

answers: So they will recognize God’s work and power to save him
So they will give him possessions
So they will make him king
medium.explanation: David wants them to know that the Lord has acted and can deliver him.
medium.q: Why does David ask that his enemies know that God’s hand has done this?

challenge.explanation: The images portray David as passing away and being tossed about.
challenge.q: What do the images of the declining shadow and the locust emphasize?

answers: His weakness and suffering explain his need for mercy and salvation
His weakness proves he needs no help
His suffering makes him stop praying
challenge.explanation: David describes his weakness as the reason he urgently needs God’s mercy and help.
challenge.q: How are David’s physical condition and his plea for deliverance connected?

answers: David asks God to act mercifully and save him
David asks his enemies to act instead of God
challenge.explanation: David appeals to God as his merciful deliverer and asks Him to save him.
challenge.q: What relationship between God and David’s situation appears in the passage?

paragraphs.title: God’s Blessing, the Enemies’ Shame, and Public Praise

easy.explanation: David says, “Let them curse, but bless thou.”
easy.q: What does David ask God to do when his enemies curse?

answers: They will immediately disappear from the land
easy.explanation: David says, “when they arise, let them be ashamed.”
easy.q: What will happen to the enemies according to David?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise him among the multitude.”
easy.q: What does David promise to do among the multitude?

answers: David is ashamed while they rejoice
They are clothed with shame, while God’s servant rejoices
Both remain in the same condition
medium.explanation: The enemies are clothed with shame, while David asks that God’s servant rejoice.
medium.q: How are David’s condition and that of his enemies reversed?

answers: The LORD stands at the right hand of the poor and saves him
His enemies commanded him to do so
medium.explanation: David praises God because He stands at the right hand of the poor to save him.
medium.q: Why does David promise to praise the LORD publicly?

medium.explanation: In this context, confusion refers to shame, humiliation, or disgrace.
medium.q: What does “confusion” mean in the phrase “let them cover themselves with their own confusion”?

answers: The curse becomes blessing and the enemies are put to shame
The blessing becomes a curse and David hides
The poor become enemies and the enemies become poor
challenge.explanation: David trusts that God will bless him while the enemies who curse him will be ashamed.
challenge.q: What is the main reversal described at the end of the psalm?

answers: His praise will be open and public
He will praise God only in his heart
He will praise God only before his enemies
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that David will praise the LORD openly before many people.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “among the multitude” add to David’s praise?

answers: God’s deliverance leads David to praise Him
Praise prevents God from helping the poor
challenge.explanation: David praises God because He stands with the poor and saves him from those who condemn him.
challenge.q: What connection is made between God’s standing at the right hand of the poor and David’s praise?
